title: Alphabet Raises AI Spending But Still Can't Meet Demand: 'We're Still in a Supply Constraint Environment'

Alphabet Inc. said demand for its artificial intelligence (AI) services continues to outpace available computing capacity despite raising its capital spending outlook.

Demand Continues to Outpace Available Capacity

The Google parent company raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to $195 billion to $205 billion, up from its prior forecast of $180 billion to $190 billion.

During Alphabet's second-quarter earnings call, CEO Sundar Pichai said Google continues to face capacity constraints as demand for AI products and cloud services exceeds available infrastructure.

"Demand for our models is translating to strong token usage across developers and enterprise customers, and we continue to be supply constrained, a sign of momentum and rapid adoption," Pichai added.

Expands Capacity to Meet AI Demand

Alphabet plans to expand its use of third-party capacity in the third quarter as a bridging strategy while it continues building out internal capacity.

"We're still in a supply constraint environment. I think we've said this now for multiple quarters in a row, we are seeing very strong demand, both from external cloud customers as well as across the business," CFO Anat Ashkenazi said.

Trending: Avoid the #1 Investing Mistake: How Your 'Safe' Holdings Could Be Costing You Big Time

Wall Street Divided on AI Spending

Alphabet's higher AI spending outlook became one of the biggest talking points after earnings, with Wall Street split between concerns over rising capital expenditures and optimism that accelerating cloud demand justifies the investment.

Investor Gary Black said the higher spending could "potentially trigger a new CapEx arms race," while Deepwater Asset Management's Gene Munster called Google Cloud's performance "the most important number" in the quarter, pointing to strong enterprise AI demand.

Earnings Beat Wall Street Estimate

Alphabet reported second-quarter revenue of $119.80 billion, topping analyst estimates of $116.82 billion, according to Benzinga Pro.

The company also reported second-quarter earnings of $9.11 per share, beating estimates of $2.87.

Alphabet Inc. 表示，尽管提高了资本支出前景，但对其人工智能 (AI) 服务的需求继续超过可用计算能力。

需求继续超过可用容量

谷歌母公司将 2026 年资本支出预期上调至 1950 亿美元至 2050 亿美元，高于之前预测的 1800 亿美元至 1900 亿美元。

在 Alphabet 第二季度财报电话会议上，首席执行官桑达尔·皮查伊 (Sundar Pichai) 表示，由于对人工智能产品和云服务的需求超过了可用基础设施，谷歌继续面临容量限制。

皮查伊补充道：“对我们模型的需求正在转化为开发商和企业客户对代币的强劲使用，而我们的供应仍然有限，这是势头和快速采用的标志。”

扩大产能以满足人工智能需求

Alphabet 计划在第三季度扩大对第三方产能的使用，作为过渡策略，同时继续建设内部产能。

“我们仍然处于供应紧张的环境中。 我认为我们已经连续多个季度这么说了，我们看到了来自外部云客户以及整个企业的非常强劲的需求。”首席财务官阿纳特·阿什肯纳齐 (Anat Ashkenazi) 说道。

趋势：避免第一大投资错误：你的“安全”持仓可能会让你付出巨大的代价

华尔街对人工智能支出存在分歧

Alphabet 较高的人工智能支出前景成为财报发布后最大的话题之一，华尔街对资本支出增加的担忧和对云需求加速证明投资合理性的乐观情绪之间存在分歧。

投资者加里·布莱克(Gary Black)表示，支出增加可能“可能引发新的资本支出军备竞赛”，而深水资产管理公司(Deepwater Asset Management)的吉恩·蒙斯特(Gene Munster)称谷歌云的业绩是本季度“最重要的数字”，指出企业人工智能需求强劲。

盈利超过华尔街预期

Benzinga Pro 的数据显示，Alphabet 第二季度营收为 1,198 亿美元，超出分析师预期的 1,168.2 亿美元。

该公司还公布第二季度每股收益 9.11 美元，超出预期的 2.87 美元。
